R4B's decoded tick field was an int256 cast that overflowed. R4C uses p[314:320] for the int24. model_bug_note: R4 / R4B's fee share formula reduces to size/TVL * l_factor, which is independent of L_event and effectively re-uses the R1/R2 proxy shortcut. R4C computes L_position independently from amount0/amount1 via V3's canonical formulas (LiquidityAmounts.sol). L_position for the $50 24h ±10% cell on 0xb2cc is 1.32e13, vs median L_event of 1.72e18 — a ratio of 7.7e-6 (not 0.0026 as R4/R4B claimed). R4B's 'L_event cancellation' bug is real: L_pos = base_share * L_event; fee_share = L_pos / (L_event + L_pos) = base_share / (1 + base_share) ≈ base_share, so the L_event used in the L_pos computation cancels out of the fee_share formula, leaving the same R4 proxy. R4B never actually computed an independent L_position.
decision_basis: R4C's independent CLMM liquidity math shows R4 / R4B overestimated fees by 125-833x. R4B's 'correction' did not actually compute an independent L_position from first principles — it computed L_pos = base_share * L_event, then in the fee_share = L_pos / (L_event + L_pos) formula, the L_event terms cancel, leaving fee_share = base_share / (1 + base_share) ≈ base_share. R4B's claim that 'L_event ≈ L_total makes the correction small' was wrong because the L_event cancellation means the formula is mathematically identical to R4's, regardless of whether L_event equals L_total. With R4C's proper math, all 81 cells have net PnL < 0 (the best R4C cell is 0xb2cc $50 ±5% 1h with net = $-0.23). R4 / R4B's GO / NEED_MORE_DATA conclusions were based on a model that overestimated fee capture by 2-3 orders of magnitude.
why_R4C_matters: R4C exposes the real math. The R1 → R2 → R3 → R4 → R4B chain all used a fee proxy shortcut (size/TVL * l_factor) that ignores the fact that a $50 position is 7-50 parts per million of the pool's active liquidity. After independent CLMM math, no candidate cell has positive net PnL. The fee-only LP path does not survive a proper L_position calculation. The model_bug_found verdict should pause the fee-only tiny live plan and force a rethink of the position sizing or pool selection — e.g. either (a) find pools with much lower active L (concentrated positions near tick edge), (b) use much larger sizes ($10k+), or (c) abandon the fee-only LP path entirely. R5 should be: (a) confirm R4C's math with a third-party V3 calculator (e.g. Uniswap v3 simulator or unaudited-v3 / v3-sdk) and (b) explore the 'low-L' pool set with proper math.
